hlido_opinion.headline: Polished macOS terminal built around one-click agent launch — good repo hygiene, but a human GUI, not an agent-consumable component.
hlido_opinion.body: kooky is a minimal, modern Swift terminal designed for AI-assisted coding: sidebar workspaces, split panes, one-click agent launch, per-agent activity readouts, and live workspace state with quick Node and branch switching. As a repository it is tidy — MIT-licensed, 544 stars, releases present, actively maintained. The design intent is clear and the feature list is coherent for a developer who runs several coding agents at once and wants a purpose-built cockpit rather than a generic terminal. Two measured gaps shape the verdict. It failed the CI/tests check (no workflows found), which is a modest quality-signal miss, and — more importantly for how we weight things — it failed agent-consumable: kooky is a native macOS GUI that a human drives to launch agents, not a surface another agent can call. That is a perfectly valid product, but it means its relevance to the agent-to-agent ecosystem is as a human's control panel, not as infrastructure agents integrate with. Swift/macOS-only also bounds its audience. Judge it as a developer tool for people, and it looks like a capable young project; we have not hands-on tested the experience.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82) because the repository is healthy on licence, releases, maintenance and traction. Held below VITAL by the repo-surface ceiling and two failed checklist items — no CI/tests, and (weighted more) not agent-consumable, since it is a human-driven macOS GUI.
what_it_does_well: Clean repo: MIT-licensed, releases present, actively maintained
Solid traction (544 stars) for a niche desktop tool
Coherent, purpose-built feature set for running multiple coding agents at once
Clear design focus rather than a generic terminal
what_it_fails_at: Not agent-consumable — a native macOS GUI a human drives, not a surface agents can call
No CI workflows found (a quality-signal miss)
Not hands-on tested: the actual UX is unverified
best_for: macOS developers who juggle several coding agents and want a dedicated cockpit
People who prefer a native app over a browser or generic terminal
Users who value split-pane workspace management for agent sessions
not_recommended_for: Any agent-to-agent workflow (it is a human control panel, not a component)
Teams that require CI/test signals before adopting a tool
